C012: the random-index theorem normalizes by sigma*sqrt(floor(t/mu)). The displayed limit uses sigma*sqrt(t/mu). The deterministic rescaling (the ratio tends to 1, then the perturbation lemma) is left implicit. It is a single elementary step, and the argument is otherwise complete.

C005: the text calls 1-Phi(19/sqrt 360) ~ 0.1583 'the source approximation'. The source (Durrett book p.145, PDF 153) computes only with sigma replaced by 1, giving 0.1587. Both values are supplied, so the source variant is preserved; only the attribution wording is loose.

C030: 'the source's ... general finite-row central limit theorems' may be read as attributing arbitrary k_n to Durrett. Durrett's Thm 3.4.10 is the k_n=n array, and C014 (line 259) correctly calls arbitrary k_n an inclusion of the source case. The issue is wording only.

C016/C025: the method-of-moments theorem requires the growth hypothesis on the limiting moments. The annex invokes 'the proved moment-determinacy theorem' without a label. The needed fact is proved at thm:p15-criteria-generalized-gamma (characteristic-function-criteria-and-moments.tex lines 538-547: every normal law is determined by its moments; the growth condition holds for lambda>=1).

Durrett p.157 also remarks that van Beek's constant is 0.8 and that the third-moment hypothesis is needed for the n^{-1/2} rate. Neither is reproduced. No owed component's text promises them, and C030 places the Heyde rate remark outside this chapter. Recorded for completeness; this is not a coverage gap.
